seminarios.titulo: Hidden symmetries in turbulence resulting from quotient-like constructions
seminarios.conteudo: I would like to discuss some non-standard constructions resembling quotient groups in the situation, when a subgroup is not normal but satisfies specific commutation relations. This situation appears in applications to turbulence, where the symmetry group under consideration is the sum of space-time scaling and Galilean groups. In this case, the subgroup of interest includes time scalings and Galilean transformations that do not commute with the evolution operator.

seminarios.titulo: Dynamics of Hénon Maps with Zero Entropy- Part 1
seminarios.conteudo:
I will focus on surface diffeomorphisms with zero entropy: Can the dynamics of these 'simple' systems be described? How does it bifurcate to positive entropy systems? These questions will be discussed for a class of volume-contracting surface diffeomorphisms whose dynamics is intermediate between one-dimensional dynamics and general surface dynamics. It includes the dynamics of any Hénon diffeomorphism with Jacobian smaller than 1/4.

In this first talk, for that type of systems, we will try to prove that any Hénon map with zero entropy and Jacobian smaller than 1/4 "is renormalizable" from a topological point of view.  This is part of a joint work with S. Crovisier and C. Tresser.
seminarios.area: Seminário de Sistemas Dinâmicos e Teoria Ergódica

seminarios.titulo: Holomorphic connections on Hopf manifolds and a new proof of Poincare-Dulac linearization theorem
seminarios.conteudo: Let H be a quotient of $C^n$ without 0 by a group Z acting by holomorphic contractions. The complex manifold H is called a Hopf manifold; it is a compact, complex, non-Kahler manifold diffeomorphic to $S^1 \times S^{n-1}$. I will prove that a Hopf manifold always admits a holomorphic connection, that is, an holomorphic covariant derivative on the tangent bundle. When the action of the contraction on $T_0C^n\ $ is non-resonant, this connection is automatically flat and torsion-free. This implies a classical theorem of Poincare, Lattes, Dulac and Sternberg about linearization of holomorphic contractions (or a contraction vector field). This is a joint work with Liviu Ornea.

seminarios.titulo: Dynamics of Hénon Maps with Zero Entropy- Part 2
seminarios.conteudo:
On the previous Monday, we were discussing that any mild dissipative dynamic of the two dimensional disc with zero entropy  (that includes the Hénon map with Jacobian smaller than 1/4) "is renormalizable" from a topological point of view.  

 

But what about its geometry? Is it bounded? In this second talk, I will discuss a work in progress with Sylvain Crovisier, Misha Lyubich and Jonguk Jang about the bounded geometry of those renormalizable systems. The proof is based on an "axiomatization of unimodal surface diffeomorphisms" that in particular, requires to develpe the notion of "critical point" for surface diffeos.  

For that type of systems, first we will try to prove that any Hénon map with zero entropy and Jacobian smaller than 1/4 "is renormalized" (this is part of joint work with S. Crovisier and C. Tresser).

 

Later, we will discuss work in progress with Sylvain Crovisier, Misha Lyubich and Jonguk Jang about the bounded geometry of those renormalizable systems.
